findings.title: Compliance rate mismatch (Results, paragraph 1 (Characteristics for the present sample))
findings.description: Three independent tool calls. grim_percentage (MCP-only, no CLI verb) shows that 70.00% at n=4494 is attainable ONLY from a count of 3146, and separately that the reported count of 3131 corresponds to 69.67%. check_summation then pins the gap at exactly 15 surveys. The figure is printed to two decimals ('70.00%'), asserting a precision the underlying ratio does not have: the true rate is 69.67%. This is a descriptive compliance statistic and no inferential claim rests on it, though the paper uses it to characterise the data as showing 'good compliance'. Most likely a rounding-then-decimal-padding slip.

findings.title: Ede composite refused
findings.description: This is the misapplication guard working as designed, not a finding against the paper. The EDE global score is the mean of four subscale means over 22 items scored 0-6, so its granularity is 1/(22*107), far finer than the printed two decimals; running GRIM with 1/n here would have manufactured an impossibility out of an ordinary value. Recorded so that the absence of a GRIM result on this row is visibly a refusal rather than an oversight.

findings.title: Table2 precision cannot determine significance
findings.description: Not an error and not a disagreement -- the reported p-values are all consistent with their printed inputs (see table2_regression_sweep). The point is that b and SE are printed to only two decimals, and at that precision the achievable p-interval for these rows spans the 0.05 threshold. A reader therefore cannot independently confirm from Table 2 that the within-person positive-affect-to-emotion-dysregulation path (bolded as significant in all six models and narrated in the Results) is significant, nor that the Model 2 within-person negative-affect indirect effect (p = .026, one of the four headline mediation claims) is. Reporting b and SE to three decimals would resolve this entirely.

findings.title: Multiplicity headline family robust
findings.description: Sensitivity analysis against the narrower and arguably more natural family definition -- one test per LOC eating dimension for the paper's central pathway. On this reading all four significant within-person mediation claims survive Benjamini-Hochberg and nothing is lost; only Bonferroni would cost the p = .026 result. Reported alongside the 24-test family so the multiplicity concern is not overstated: the paper's core within-person conclusion is robust to correction, its between-person and secondary claims are not.

findings.title: Duplication no independent overlap
findings.description: NO duplication anomaly. The tool reports zero improbable cross-independent-source overlap. All 15 flagged patterns are same-sample repeats and are expected by construction: the six models are fitted to the SAME 107 participants and share an identical negative-affect-to-emotion-dysregulation submodel, so the a-path reproduces to two decimals across models. The largest cluster (Models 4 and 6, six matching pairs) likewise reflects a shared submodel plus two-decimal rounding of genuinely different quantities. The aggregate severity is the tool's 'indeterminate' owing to the same-sample caveat, not evidence of copying. This entry records that the check ran and cleared.

findings.title: No power analysis reported (Statistical Analyses section (whole))
findings.description: No a-priori power analysis or sample-size justification is offered and the sample size is inherited from the parent trial, so verify_power_analysis has nothing to reproduce -- I did not supply invented inputs to force an answer. Worth recording because the between-person half of every model is estimated from 107 level-2 units, and the between-person estimates are exactly where the paper's results are least stable: standard errors of 0.38-0.53 on coefficients of 0.34-0.89, with one result at p = .052 and another at p = .055. findings.title: Trial registry id malformed (Participants and Procedures, first paragraph)
findings.description: Manual textual observation; no tool and no arithmetic involved. ClinicalTrials.gov identifiers are NCT plus eight digits; the string printed here carries seven, so it is one character short and will not resolve as written. Almost certainly a dropped digit in typesetting rather than anything substantive, but it defeats the purpose of quoting a registration number: a reader cannot retrieve the parent trial's registered protocol or pre-specified outcomes, which is the only route to checking whether these six MSEMs were pre-specified or exploratory. The paper is a secondary analysis and makes no pre-registration claim of its own.

findings.title: Data availability on request (Data Availability Statement)
findings.description: Recorded factually rather than as a criticism. This is participant-level momentary data from a clinical trial in a stigmatised diagnostic group, so restricted access is defensible and this is NOT the state-but-withhold pattern of rulebook rule 7 (the paper does not claim the data are included). It does mean that none of the reconstructions this sweep could not perform -- the level-1 N, the mediation product terms, confidence intervals for the null claims -- can be resolved by a reader without contacting the authors.
